derby.heading: Derby, from a shop that was the first one here
derby.categoryCopy: Derby is where this shop started: we were the first roller derby shop to open in South Africa, and Roadhouse Roller Rink still names us its recommended shop. Eight products sit under Roller Derby itself, but the derby kit is spread across the shop — 27 protective sets, 38 wheels and bearings lines, 17 toe stops and jam plugs. The question is almost never which shop. It is which boot fits your foot, which plate fits that boot, and which wheels suit the floor you actually skate on. Work it in that order, and tell us what you skate: we will go through it with you.

faq.a: Measure, do not guess. Heel to wall, standing, both feet, and use the larger one — the Size Finder walks you through it and gives you the size in the brand's own scale. Two honest warnings. Brands differ by 1-2 full sizes for the same foot, so a number off a chart is a starting point, not a fitting. And our size chart carries no table at all for Riedell or Sure-Grip, which are brands a derby skater may well end up in. For those, send us the measurement on WhatsApp and we size you by hand.

faq.q: Which plate size for my boot?
faq.a: Plates are sized by wheelbase — axle to axle — against the boot, not by your shoe size. We publish the Pilot F-16 chart on our size chart page: plate sizes 5.0 to 8.5, mapped onto Q-4/Q-6, F-1 and Jackson boot sizes, with plate lengths from 218 mm to 309 mm. Check the size with us before you order. For Roll-Line there is no plate-to-boot table published anywhere we could find, so that one is a WhatsApp conversation: send us the boot and its size and we work it out with you.

faq.q: What wheel hardness do I want for Roadhouse versus tarmac?
faq.a: The principle first, because the principle is the part that is always true. A softer compound grips and absorbs, which is what a rough outdoor surface takes out of you; a harder compound slides and rolls faster, which is what a smooth indoor floor rewards. What we will not do is put a number on this page. The right hardness for the floor at Roadhouse, and for the stretch of tarmac outside your house, depends on that surface, on your weight and on how you skate — and it is Melony who confirms it, not a chart. Tell us where you skate and what you weigh, on WhatsApp, and we will pick the set with you.

faq.q: What does a league kit list need?
faq.a: The standard derby set is six things: skates, helmet, knee pads, elbow pads, wrist guards and a mouthguard. We carry 27 protective sets, and we would rather build the kit with you than hand you a list — we will tell you straight what we hold and what we bring in. Four South African leagues are running that we know of: Golden City Rollers, Durban Roller Derby, Cape Town Rollergirls and P-Town Roller Derby. What each one requires we are not going to guess at. Per-league kit lists are coming in the build; until then, tell us which league you are joining and we will work through it with you.

sizes.hint: Aura sizes are in millimetres. The Sky 100 runs 210-285 men's, 210-280 women's.
sizes.brannockNote: Aura sizes from the Brannock suggested size, which is a high-performance fit. Want it roomier? Add half a size — 5 mm. And if a boot feels tight, go up in width before you go up in length.

pdp.fitNote: This is a carbon boot, and Aura builds it to fit very snug before it is moulded. That is not a sizing error, it is the design: the carbon expands in width and volume onto your foot once it has been warmed. The heat-mould is not an upgrade on these — Aura publishes it as a requirement, so plan for it. We size from the Brannock suggested size rather than raw foot length. That suggested size is the high-performance fit; add half a size, 5 mm, if you want a comfort fit. And the rule we hold to at the bench is Aura's own: if the boot feels tight, move up in width before you add length. Width first, length second. Because we import this boot specifically for you, we confirm the size with you on WhatsApp before anything is ordered.
pdp.specTableNote: Boot only — blades are sold separately. Level and stiffness are not published anywhere we could reach, so they are left out rather than guessed. Which sizes and widths we can actually order is the one line Melony still confirms.

demoSheet.title: This cart is a demo
demoSheet.body: Cart and checkout land in month 1 of the build. Today this boot is ordered the way Mel's orders everything: one WhatsApp message. Tap below and the boot and your selected size are already in it.

qa.a: We warm the boot until the carbon softens, you stand in it in the sock you skate in, and it cools onto your heel, your instep and your ankle. On an Aura it is not a luxury step: Aura publishes the mould as a requirement. On the live site that is a phone call to the shop. Here you book it with the fitting and it happens in the same appointment.

Before we order, nothing is committed — we only place the order once you have confirmed the size with us on WhatsApp, and that confirmation is the moment that matters. After we have ordered, the boot is being brought into the country for you specifically, so we are not going to print a policy here that we have not agreed with you. Message us and we will tell you honestly where the order has got to. Cancelling a fitting rather than a boot is simpler, and that policy is on the booking page.
Then we exchange it. In full, the terms we are proposing:
qa.aAfter: The carve-out is the line that matters on this boot, and it is why we confirm your size on WhatsApp before we order.

measure.heading: Measure heel to wall
measure.lede: Two minutes, a sheet of paper and a pencil. Do it standing — your foot spreads under your own weight, and that is the foot the boot has to fit.
steps: Put a sheet of paper on a hard floor, one short edge tight against the wall.
Stand on it with your heel against the wall and your weight on that foot.
Mark the paper at the end of your longest toe. That is not always the big toe.
Measure from the wall edge to the mark, in millimetres.
Now do the other foot. Feet differ. Use the larger number.
measure.altInputsLabel: Or start from something you already know
measure.altOwnSkateHint: Brand and size. What is wrong with the pair you have is the most useful thing you can tell us.

whichSky.heading: Which Sky?
whichSky.instruction: Aura makes three Sky boots and its own chart picks between them. We need three things: your foot length in millimetres, your body weight, and whether you jump.
whichSky.note: This step is straight off Aura's selection chart. It is their matrix, not our opinion.

handoffs.noTableHeading: Some brands we stock have no table we can size you from
handoffs.noTable: We would rather say so than compute a number out of nothing. Roll-Line, one of our two flagship lines, publishes no size table anywhere we could find. Riedell has a tab on our size chart, but it sends you off to Riedell's own pages, and one of those links is broken as we published it. Sure-Grip's tab carries our own measuring method and a printable insole chart on our domain — the most personal sizing content on the site, and also the one thing a calculator cannot read. For any of those, send us your measurement on WhatsApp and we size you ourselves.

booking.heading: Come and have skates put on your feet
booking.lede: Four kinds of appointment, all by appointment, all with a person who skates. Durations and prices carry the proposed stamp because Mel publishes no fitting menu today.

intake.heading: Before you come
intake.lede: None of this is compulsory. All of it makes the appointment shorter and the fit better.
items: Measure both feet at home if you can — heel to wall, standing, in millimetres. Bring the numbers.
Wear or bring the socks you skate in. Sock thickness changes the size.
Bring your current skates if you own a pair, even wrong ones. What is wrong with them is the most useful thing you can tell us.
For an ice fitting, bring your blades if you already own them.
For a video consult, have paper, a pen, a tape measure, a wall and a hard floor ready before we call.
